messages:
maya: Quick sync — Optimize toolkit prioritization. Customers keep asking for quantization profiles, smarter batching, and prefix KV caching. We can't do all at once. Need proposed ordering + launch criteria. Prefer RICE or impact/effort?

alex: +1 to RICE for a first pass. Quick proposed numbers to start convo:
```
Feature | Reach | Impact | Confidence | Effort(days)
Quantization | 200 | 3 | 0.7 | 30
Batching | 350 | 2 | 0.6 | 20
Caching | 150 | 4 | 0.5 | 25
```

sanjay: math time. RICE_score = (Reach * Impact * Confidence) / Effort
Quant: (200*3*0.7)/30 = 14
Batch: (350*2*0.6)/20 = 21
Cache: (150*4*0.5)/25 = 12
So that raw view puts batching first, then quant, then caching.

emily: caveat: batching has infra complexity (per-tenant fairness, per-model kv lifetime, backpressure). Effort likely +10 days vs table. Also gains depend on request distribution — e.g., short chat vs long completions behave differently.

raj: from SEs/customer side: caching (prefix + KV) often gives the biggest p99 wins for chat-heavy products because repeated prefixes are common. Caching is also easier as an opt-in layer on top of existing runtime. Could do a small MVP with TTLs and simple LFU/LRU.

linda: finance quick note: if batching yields 20% token reduction in effective compute, that's ~15-25% cost improvement depending on model/instance. We should quantify assumed $/token and annualize for sales conversations.

maya: good points. Proposal: hybrid sequence to reduce risk:
1) Batching MVP focused on single-tenant pinned workloads (min infra changes, deliverable fast)
2) Quantization profiles for top N models + eval harness and rollback criteria
3) Opt-in prefix caching (customer-configurable TTLs + simple eviction)

product-bot: action created: OPT-78 "Batching MVP" assigned to @emily — due 2025-10-15

emily: I'll scope MVP: continuous host-level batching + per-model batch heuristics + config flags. No per-tenant fairness in MVP. Rough estimate 25 dev days + 5 infra days for testing and rollout.

sanjay: quant notes: need eval harness + representative prompt sets. Quality delta threshold proposal: no >1% drop in top-line eval metric OR <3% increase in human-failure rate on holdout prompts. Use canary rollout at 5%-25%.

maya: draft launch criteria (for each feature):
- p95 latency within SLA (hosted) on target traffic profile
- throughput improvement >= 30% OR cost per token down >= 15% (whichever maps to business metric)
- quality regressions <= 1% on eval suite and no customer regressions in canary
- docs + SDK flags + migration notes

alex: sequencing note: ship batching-MVP -> monitor unit economics + QA signals -> ship quant profiles -> follow with caching as Q1 follow-up. This helps us learn the real-world batching lift before we invest heavy infra.

raj: agree. Also strongly recommend 3 customer pilots (one high-throughput chat, one enterprise with long sequences, one embeddings-heavy) per phase to validate assumptions.

maya: action items:
- emily: finalize batching MVP spec + prod plan (due EOD next Tue)
- sanjay: draft quant eval thresholds + rollout plan
- raj: draft pilot customer list & SE-runbooks
- linda/alex: we'll model basic unit-econ scenarios for the roadmap review

maya: I'll update the roadmap doc and keep the RICE table as a living doc. Thanks all :tada:
